title: The Markov Equation: Complete Classification via Vieta Jumping
description: A fully verified, axiom-free proof that every positive solution of the Markov equation x² + y² + z² = 3xyz lies in the Markov tree rooted at the singular solution (1,1,1). The classification is proved by infinite descent: sort a triple, then Vieta-jump its maximal coordinate to strictly decrease the coordinate sum. Includes the Vieta-jump involution, the descent inequality 3xy − z < z, uniqueness of the singular solution, and a reachability relation generated by transpositions and Vieta moves.

crossReferences.description: Both are quadratic Diophantine equations solved by descent along a solution-preserving involution. Pell's x² − Dy² = 1 uses multiplication by the fundamental unit; the Markov equation uses Vieta jumping z ↦ 3xy − z, which is the ternary analogue of the conjugation that swaps the two roots of a quadratic.

The descent engine is precisely Vieta's formulas for the quadratic t² − 3xy·t + (x²+y²) whose two roots z, z' = 3xy − z satisfy z + z' = 3xy and z·z' = x² + y². Fixing two coordinates turns the Markov equation into this quadratic in the third.

overview.historicalContext: Andrey Markov introduced the equation x² + y² + z² = 3xyz in 1879–1880 while studying the minima of indefinite binary quadratic forms. Its positive integer solutions, the Markov triples (1,1,1), (1,1,2), (1,2,5), (1,5,13), (2,5,29), …, organize into an infinite ternary tree: starting from the singular solution (1,1,1), every triple is obtained by repeatedly replacing one coordinate z by its Vieta partner 3xy − z. The Markov numbers (coordinates appearing in some triple) govern the Lagrange spectrum below 3 and are the subject of the famous open Markov uniqueness conjecture. The tree structure itself, proved here, is the classical foundation due to Markov and Frobenius.
overview.problemStatement: Classify all positive integer solutions of x² + y² + z² = 3xyz. Concretely: show that every such triple can be reduced to the root (1,1,1) by a finite sequence of coordinate transpositions and Vieta jumps z ↦ 3xy − z — i.e. every Markov triple lies in the Markov tree.
overview.proofStrategy: Infinite descent on the coordinate sum x + y + z (a positive integer). Given a triple, sort it to x ≤ y ≤ z using at most three transpositions (sort_reachable). If z = 1 then x = y = z = 1 and we are at the root. Otherwise z ≥ 2, and the Vieta jump on the maximal coordinate produces a genuine Markov triple (x, y, 3xy − z) with a strictly smaller sum, by the descent inequality 3xy − z < z. Strong induction on the sum then reduces every triple to (1,1,1).
keyInsights: Fixing x and y, the Markov equation is a monic quadratic in z: t² − 3xy·t + (x² + y²) = 0. Its two roots z and z' satisfy z + z' = 3xy and z·z' = x² + y² (Vieta). Hence z' = 3xy − z is again a (positive) solution: the Vieta jump. It is an involution, so the move relation is symmetric and generates a tree.

The descent inequality is the arithmetic heart. For a sorted triple x ≤ y ≤ z, evaluating the quadratic at t = y gives g(y) = (y − z)(y − z') = x² + 2y² − 3xy² = x² + y²(2 − 3x) ≤ 0 (since x ≥ 1). With y ≤ z this forces z' ≤ y ≤ z, so replacing the maximal coordinate never increases — and in fact strictly decreases — the sum.

Strictness uses that z ≥ 2 forces y < z: a tie y = z would give x² = z²(3x − 2), impossible for 1 ≤ x ≤ z and z ≥ 2. Then x² + y² = z·z' ≤ z·y < z², which converts (using 3xyz = x² + y² + z² < 2z² and z > 0) into 3xy < 2z, i.e. 3xy − z < z.

The singular solution (1,1,1) is the unique fixed triple of the descent and the unique triple with all coordinates equal: (t,t,t) is Markov iff t²(t−1) = 0 iff t = 1. Every other triple has a strict maximum that can be jumped down, so the descent terminates only at the root.

Reachability is formalized as the reflexive-transitive closure of a three-constructor move relation (two transpositions and one Vieta jump). Because all descent moves go strictly downward in the sum, the classification needs no symmetry of the relation — a single downward ReflTransGen chain from any triple to (1,1,1) suffices.

conclusion.summary: A self-contained, 0-axiom, 0-sorry formalization (237 lines, 17 theorems, 3 definitions) proving the classical structure theorem for the Markov equation: the positive solutions form a tree rooted at (1,1,1), with every triple reachable by Vieta jumping and transpositions. The descent inequality and the Vieta-jump involution are proved from scratch over ℤ; nothing is assumed beyond Mathlib's order and ring infrastructure.
conclusion.implications: The tree structure is the entry point to Markov theory: the Markov numbers it generates form the discrete part of the Lagrange spectrum below 3, and the still-open Markov uniqueness conjecture asks whether each Markov number determines its triple uniquely. The descent technique here (Vieta jumping) is the same method used in olympiad-famous problems and in the arithmetic of other ternary Diophantine equations.
openQuestions: Markov uniqueness conjecture: is every Markov number the largest coordinate of exactly one Markov triple? This remains open and is not addressed here.
Quantitative tree growth: the number of Markov triples with maximal coordinate ≤ N grows like (log N)², a refinement orthogonal to the structural classification proved here.

Generalized Markov equations x² + y² + z² = 3xyz + k and Markov–Hurwitz equations in more variables admit analogous (but more delicate) descent trees; formalizing those would reuse the Vieta-jump infrastructure built here.
